items.title: David Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2022
items.q: So we got Pete La Roca and James Spaulding... And Pete La Roca and James Spaulding were great. And that’s what started it. It morphed into what the Cookers are today

ctx.x: I understand the group came out of a Freddie Hubbard connection. But I wonder if at some point, did you feel not — intimidated isn’t the right word. Was it a bit odd for you to be the head of a group where the majority of the players were anywhere from twenty to almost thirty years older than you? Now you had established yourself certainly as a presence in New York and had your due respect. But still, I’m wondering if any of this has been odd for you to sort of be in charge of musicians of that pedigree?

Well there’s many things I could say about that. I did work with Freddie Hubbard for eight years before — I guess they kind of overlapped a little bit. And the first night of the Cookers gig, or the first attempt at it, was something they asked me to put together because of my connection with Freddie. The guy wanted Freddie to come and like be the emcee, you know. The Night of the Cookers concert I don’t remember the exact dates, but they are right around Freddie’s birthday, and there was this club in Brooklyn…

some more Freddie Hubbard alumni. Ronnie Mathews did it and Kiane Zawadi did it. And that concert was a success. And Pete La Roca and James Spaulding were great. And that’s what started it. It morphed into what the Cookers are today, but it started as this Night of the Cookers celebration, that people reached out to me because at the time I was working with Freddie, and, you know, they thought I can help get them to do something Freddie didn’t really want to do which was come fly to New York to blow out a…
